correctness.rationale: For W_n=K_n corona K1 (n>=2), classify each core-leaf pair as empty, core-only, leaf-only or both. With >=2 empty pairs the two uncolored cores permanently block any blue core, even after all available leaf forces. With exactly one empty pair and no initial blue leaf every black core has two white neighbors (missing core and own leaf), so stalled. With one empty and a blue leaf, all leaf-only pairs first activate their core, a core whose leaf is already blue forces the unique missing core, and the new core forces its pendant; remaining whites are forced. With no empty pairs all initial leaf-only states activate cores, which force all remaining white leaves. This complete case split gives polynomial (2x+x²)^n+n((2x+x²)^(n-1)-x^(n-1)), Z=n-1, minimum-set count n(2^(n-1)-1) and total (n+3)3^(n-1)-n. The actual artifacts/verify.py Git blob was read; a separately implemented brute zero forcing simulation exactly matched polynomial coefficients for n=2,3,4,5. Infinite theorem follows from structural four-state proof, not finite tests.
